title: parseTrailerPlan refuses every wrong-typed patch value
body:
## Summary
The trailer plan door cast a model's patch to BeatPatch without checking value types; `raises: "scale"` crashed the checker.

## Description
lib/script/trailer/plan.ts parseTrailerPlan checked keys only ("value types are the schema's request, not a guarantee"); the explainer twin parseEditPlan was fixed in de743e2a. Now one PATCH_PROPERTIES table feeds the schema and the parser; `promises` (never in the schema) is refused.

## Flow
- model plan {raises:"scale"} -> parseTrailerPlan ok -> replayTrailerPlan -> runStructureCheck -> TypeError in checkEscalation

## Expected impact
A wrong-typed model plan is refused with its field named. Could break: none - no production caller.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the door reads what it admits
Before: 48 wrong-typed values: 0 refused, 48 accepted, 15 threw
After: 39 over the declared fields: 39 refused, 0 threw
Method: gate - check:trailer-structure plan cases, seeded red on HEAD plan.ts
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: lib/script/trailer/plan.ts parseTrailerPlan (HEAD): patch: o.patch as BeatPatch

After: NaN: pass=0 unmeasured=2; Infinity: pass=0 violation=0

title: Both production cut-log readers hand-roll logFromRecord, and default head to 0 where it defaults to every op
body:
## Summary
lib/producers/script.ts:186 and app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/realScript.ts:24 build a CutLog inline instead of calling ops.ts logFromRecord.

## Description
logFromRecord (lib/script/trailer/ops.ts:138-149) requires an ops array, clamps head to [0, ops.length], defaults a missing head to ops.length and a missing originBudget to the record's budget. Both readers write `ops: st.ops ?? [], head: st.head ?? 0` and pass originBudget raw. A record with ops and no head derives with ZERO edits applied on both real halves, and one with no originBudget derives budget undefined (editAllowance then reads `.assets` of undefined). out-of-scope: bound-producers and part-port-real-and-contract own the two sites.

## Flow
- record {cut, budget, origin, ops:[op], head absent} -> cutLogOf -> derive -> the creator's edit is not applied
- fix: both readers call logFromRecord(written(st))

## Expected impact
One reading of a stored cut on every half. Could break: a record whose head is intentionally absent (none written today).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule, one implementation
Before: 3 readers, 2 defaulting head to 0 vs 1 to ops.length (code read)
After: 1 reader (predicted)
Method: simulation - both sites are in other contexts' paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/producers/script.ts:186 written<CutLog>({ ..., ops: st["ops"] ?? [], head: st["head"] ?? 0 }); app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/realScript.ts:24 same; lib/script/trailer/ops.ts:147 head default rec.ops.length
instrument: a probe: the same stored record (ops present, head absent; originBudget absent) through cutLogOf, realScript's reader and logFromRecord -> derive() equal on all three

## Description

## Expected impact

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a dropped edit is reported
Before: 2 of 2 callers discard skipped (code read)
After: 0 of 2 (predicted)
Method: simulation - sites out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a producer-step case: compose cut, edit a beat, recompose without it -> the step's record or outcome names the skipped op (today: nothing)

title: atSeconds reads 0:75 as 75 seconds, and the kernel holds a verbatim twin
body:
## Summary
lib/script/trailer/types.ts atSeconds accepts any digit run per field, so '0:75', '1:5' and '1:60:00' parse instead of returning null.

## Description
Its doc says 'm:ss or h:mm:ss ... null rather than guessing'; a seconds field over 59 is a guess. packages/kernel/src/records/digest.ts:48 secondsAt is the same body (cites atSeconds), so tightening one alone forks the runtime digest from the cut's clock - the fix is a pair change across lib/ and packages/kernel (another context).

## Flow
- beat at '0:75' -> atSeconds 75 -> shot lane and scriptView place it at 1:15
- fix: every field after the first is two digits < 60, in both copies

## Expected impact
A mistyped timecode is reported (atS null) instead of silently placed. Could break: stored beats with such marks (none in fixtures: git grep shows only well-formed m:ss).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality
Before: atSeconds('0:75')=75, ('1:5')=65, ('1:60:00')=7200
After: null x3 (predicted)
Method: probe - scratch tsx over the current function for Before; After unbuilt because of the kernel twin
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/script/trailer/types.ts atSeconds: /^\d+$/ per part; packages/kernel/src/records/digest.ts:48-58 secondsAt identical
instrument: a seam case in check:trailer-structure plus a kernel vitest asserting both parsers agree on ['0:75','1:5','1:60:00','1:02','1:00:00']

After: 1 advisory row per spent promise (predicted)
Method: simulation - verdict choice left to the worker
Result: better
